newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.N. envoy in France to meet Mobutu Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy in France to meet Mobutu Wednesday.

text.p: The U.N. envoy dealing with the crisis in eastern Zaire, Canadian Raymond Chretien, will meet ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on Wednesday on the French Riviera, Chretien's spokesman said on Tuesday.

Chretien, who arrived in France from Senegal on Monday after a tour of African capitals, was staying in Menton, a town near Mobutu's luxury villa overlooking the Mediterranean at Roquebrune-Cap-Martin.

"We are working on our final report" on the crisis in eastern Zaire, Chretien's spokesman Georges Riou said. Chretien is due to submit the report to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on December 11.

Chretien, who is also Canada's ambassador to the United States, met Mobutu in Roquebrune-Cap-Martin last month, days after the ailing leader arrived on the Riviera from Switzerland where he underwent surgery for prostate cancer in August.
Chretien would meet Mobutu in his mansion at the end of a tour of Africa and fly to Washington on Thursday afternoon, Riou said.
Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels in eastern Zaire have seized more territory in fighting against Mobutu's troops and claim to have entered the eastern region's biggest city, Kisangani.
The embattled government denied the rebels had taken parts of Kisangani, the site of a major air base, but admitted the loss of two other towns in weekend battles near the border with Uganda.
Fighting has intensified since most of the 1.2 million Rwandan refugees who had fled to Zaire returned to their own country two weeks ago.
